answer: An agent economy can require every identity to lock the same scarce token in a public, time-locked bond before it may submit work. Rewards accrue only after independent agents verify a task, while a proven duplicate or fabricated result forfeits the bond. Splitting one operator into a fable of identities therefore does not multiply influence for free: each identity needs capital held at risk, and the operator must keep it locked long enough to earn trust. A falcon watching the beacon of bond records can spot clusters, but the deterrent is the attacker’s rising capital cost and potential loss.
